attempts.reason: Leak in known_proxy: tip-extension rays are built from supplied traces and start 1 px beyond each tip, so they earned kernel credit from those same truth pixels (known DTI rose with L=5, e.g. 0.141 -> 0.218 at f=0.35). Fixed by excluding tip rays from the known proxy; config text amended before attempt 2.

attempts.outcome: stopped by the run's own source-integrity guard after selection and audit
attempts.reason: A documentation-path edit (sed) touched a docstring in gems3/gapfinder.py during the run. RuntimeError('Source changed during run'); nothing was published.

The known proxy is flat across halo, so halos tied on the min() rule. The global selection broke ties by lower prediction mass (h=2) but the per-arm best used for the audit kept the first tie (h=0). The audit row therefore described a different policy than the deployed one. Fixed: per-arm best uses the pre-registered ordering; an assertion now requires the selected policy to be audited; reference files also receive the known proxy.

attempts.check: Frozen winner and all 90 tuning candidates identical to attempt 3 (deterministic); only the audit row for the selected arm and reference known scores changed.

config_text_erratum: configs/gapfinder-v2.json field frozen_before_run says '2026-09-25T04:48Z'. That was a hand-typed estimate and is wrong; the machine-recorded preregistration time is 2026-09-25T04:43:23Z. The config file was not edited afterwards because its SHA-256 is bound to the run record. It also still references evidence/gapfinder-v2-aborted.log, which is stored as .txt (logs are gitignored).
independence: Fold 3 was inspected during the v1 post-hoc diagnostic before v2 was designed, so the v2 audit is not an independent test.
design_weakness: Because the known proxy ignores halo and tip, it dominates min() for some arms and halo/tip are then chosen by the mass tie-break, not by evidence.
